summary: Jessica Sanders recounts running her first marathon, the Horizon City Marathon on September 10, 2023. Inspired by colleague Lucas Bennett and coached by Karen Smith, she trained for five months, recovered from a July sprained ankle, battled self-doubt, and hit the wall at mile 20. She finished, finding meaning in the shared stories of fellow runners and the supportive marathon culture.
one_line: Jessica Sanders narrates training for and finishing the Horizon City Marathon on September 10, 2023, overcoming injury, doubt, and the wall.
key_facts: Jessica Sanders ran her first marathon, the Horizon City Marathon, on September 10, 2023.
Lucas Bennett, a long-time marathoner and Jessica Sanders's colleague at Johnston & Hastings, planted the idea of running a marathon during a casual lunch break.
Lucas Bennett said: "Running a marathon is like life condensed into a few hours—you face your doubts, you push through pain, and if you keep going, you emerge stronger."
In April 2023 Jessica Sanders would not have considered running a marathon.
Coach Karen Smith designed a rigorous training program, giving Jessica Sanders only five months to go from casual jogger to marathon runner.
In July Jessica Sanders suffered a sprained ankle that threatened to derail her training, but fellow runners offered advice and encouragement.
To fight self-doubt about covering 26.2 miles, Jessica Sanders listened to podcasts, read articles, and talked to seasoned marathoners.
The 'taper' is the period of scaled-back training before the marathon, allowing the body to recover and the mind to prepare.
Race day was clear and cool; Lucas Bennett reminded Jessica Sanders of their training mantra, "your race, your pace."
Jessica Sanders hit the 'wall' at mile 20, with her legs screaming and lungs burning.
During the final 6.2 miles she saw a cancer survivor and a woman running in memory of a lost loved one among the runners.
Spectator signs included "Pain is temporary, pride is forever" and "Run if you can, walk if you must, but finish no matter what."
Jessica Sanders finished and received a medal, which she describes as a reminder of perseverance.
